title: Private/VPC on-prem release coordination for RBAC, Audit Logging, and KMS
creator: Maya Patel
summary: Coordinated product launch activities for Private/VPC and on-prem features: role-based access control (RBAC), tenant audit logging, and KMS integrations. Primary goals are synchronized release notes, technical enablement for SEs, legal/compliance sign-off, and cross-team go-to-market readiness.
acceptance_criteria: RBAC APIs and console flows documented in release notes and admin guide
Audit logging schema confirmed with Security and available in customer logs endpoint
KMS integration steps validated for AWS KMS and customer-managed HSMs
Release notes reviewed by legal and security and published to docs site
Enablement training delivered to sales, solutions engineering, and support
Rollout checklist executed for both hosted and private control plane customers
primary_tasks: Consolidate technical release notes draft covering RBAC, audit logging schema, KMS modes
Coordinate API changelog entries with runtime and SDK teams
Schedule and run enablement webinar for SEs and early customers
Prepare step-by-step KMS onboarding playbook for private installs
Work with Docs to publish admin migration guide and FAQs
Obtain security and legal sign-off on retention & consent language for audit logs
Create Support runbook with triage flows and escalation contacts
Finalize release communication cadence and customer advisory templates
release_notes_draft: Highlights: Launching RBAC controls, tenant-scoped audit logs, and customer KMS integrations for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments.
RBAC: New roles and permission matrix for admin, operator, auditor; SCIM sync notes and migration tips.
Audit logs: JSON schema v1 with event types, retention knobs, and export endpoints. Examples included.
KMS: Support for envelope encryption with AWS KMS and customer HSMs; key rotation guidance and failure modes.
Compatibility: Backwards-compatible defaults for hosted customers; optional flags for private installers.
Security & Compliance: Data residency notes and recommended retention policies; legal approval reference SEC-134.
rollout_steps: Freeze final docs and release notes one business day prior to publication
Deploy server-side feature flags in staging and run smoke tests with SE team
Enable canary release to selected private customers with support on standby
Open public docs and update Console help text concurrently with GA
Announce GA to existing private customers via account teams and publish advisory
Collect first-week telemetry on API errors, auth failures, and KMS timeouts
communications_calendar: 2026-03-16: Docs publish and enablement webinar for SEs (recording available)
2026-03-17: Customer advisory email to private customers with opt-in canary
2026-03-20: GA announcement and release notes posted
2026-03-27: Follow-up health check with top 10 private customers
enablement_plan: SE Workshop: hands-on lab for provisioning RBAC roles and verifying audit logs
Support Playbook: step-by-step troubleshooting guide for KMS errors and log ingestion
Sales One-Pager: TL;DR of benefits, supported compliance regimes, and lift estimates
Training Recording: 45-minute session with demo and FAQ; host Q&A in Slack channel #private-launch
Office Hours: twice-weekly for first two sprints after GA to triage onboarding issues
risks_mitigations: Risk: Customers misconfigure KMS and lose access. Mitigation: Provide clear preflight checklist and validation script; require backup key access instructions.
Risk: Audit logging volume causes unexpected storage costs. Mitigation: Recommend retention defaults, provide sampling/ingestion knobs and cost calculator.
Risk: RBAC migration creates permission gaps. Mitigation: Provide migration tool and dry-run mode; SE review for high-risk customers.
Risk: Delayed legal sign-off. Mitigation: escalate early, surface tradeoffs, include provisional wording in release notes until final approval
metrics_success_criteria: <5% support tickets related to initial RBAC/KMS onboarding in first 30 days
Audit log ingestion error rate <1% post-GA
Average KMS call latency within SLO (<250ms) for 95th percentile
>80% SEs report readiness after enablement session (survey)
Two enterprise customers complete private onboarding in first month
